title: A famous clock
visual_consistency: A continuous London public-time sequence built around the same famous stone clock tower beside the Houses of Parliament. Whenever the clock face is visible, make it a simplified blank cream face with only two dark hands; do not draw numerals, Roman numerals, tick marks, minute marks, symbols, decorative letters, or readable clock markings. Keep a warm historic-city atmosphere near the river, subtle broadcast sound-wave metaphors with no logos, calm observatory/timekeeping officials, and one ordinary painter whose accidental paint pot creates the final comic reversal. No readable signs, plaques, maps, posters, logos, clock numbers, captions, labels, UI panels, speech bubbles, letters, or words anywhere in the images.

frames.prompt: Frame 1 of a continuous London public-time story in a wide horizontal composition: a young visitor and a parent stand near the river looking up at the same famous stone clock tower beside the Houses of Parliament. The clock face is visible but deliberately simplified as a blank cream circle with only two dark hands; no numerals, no Roman numerals, no tick marks, no minute marks, no symbols. Subtle glowing sound waves travel outward from the tower toward distant small radio-listening silhouettes in warm windows, showing that the chimes can be heard far away. Grand but gentle educational mood, no readable signs, no logos, no text.

Suggest observatory timekeeping through instruments and careful posture only, with no maps, labels, logos, charts, numerals, or readable text.

High on the tower, an ordinary painter working carefully has accidentally hung a small paint pot from one of the large clock hands, weighing it down in a clear but non-destructive comic way. Below, small officials and passers-by react with surprised concern. The painter looks embarrassed, not malicious. The clock face is a simplified blank cream circle with only two dark hands; no numerals, no Roman numerals, no tick marks, no minute marks, no symbols.
